content.title: Zeplin between the design file and the code
content.body: Zeplin is filed in this repository as a design handoff and collaboration platform for designers and developers, and every record held for it describes the same narrow position: the step after a design is finished. The design software guide records teams built around Sketch's plugin-dependent model, listing Abstract for version control, Anima for prototyping, and Zeplin for handoff; two further guides describe the same gap that a handoff tool exists to fill. Nothing in the dataset describes Zeplin producing designs, so this page treats it as the receiving end of a design workflow rather than part of the drawing surface itself.

content.title: CSS properties and component specifications
content.body: The concrete job recorded for Zeplin appears in this repository's collaboration write-up, which states the problem from the developer's side: developers cannot inspect CSS properties or component specifications through Sketch's native viewer, and third-party tools like Zeplin are required for developer handoff. That sentence is effectively the product's brief — the specifications behind a finished screen, in a form someone can build from, without the design file itself becoming the delivery mechanism. Two further entries repeat the arrangement, recording Sketch's handoff as its inspection panel plus an integration with tools such as Zeplin, which is the same workflow described from the other end.

content.title: The Sketch workflow our guides describe
content.body: Zeplin is rarely described alone in this repository, because the guides discuss it as one part of a workflow that has accreted around Sketch. The design software guide is explicit about the trade that comes with it: teams built around that plugin-dependent model can be highly productive, which is also a description of how much would have to be rebuilt if the stack changed. The parts of the recorded workflow are:
items: Abstract, named for version control in a Sketch-centered workflow
Anima, named for prototyping in that same workflow
Zeplin, named for handoff at the end of it
Sketch's inspection panel, recorded as the native handoff route
Third-party handoff where the native viewer stops short of specifications

content.title: The recorded band of $17-29/mo
content.body: This page records Zeplin as freemium with a list band of $17-29/mo, and that band does specific work in this repository's comparison data: the starting-price row is marked in Zeplin's favor against Figma and against InVision, and no other price figure for the product is stored anywhere in the dataset. The band is therefore both the only number on file and unconfirmed by a second source, which is a weaker position than a figure repeated across pages. Treat it as a starting point recorded on this page rather than a quote, and check the vendor's current pricing before building a budget on it.

content.title: Where Zeplin does not reach
content.body: Three limits follow from the position the records give it. It sits downstream of design work: the repository describes Zeplin receiving finished screens for handoff, so a team looking for a place to draw has to look elsewhere, and the comparison field reinforces that by matching it against design tools it does not lead. Our records also hold nothing about what the product produces beyond specifications — no file formats, no export paths, and no design-surface features appear in the dataset under this name. And the workflow it is recorded inside is Sketch's, which means its relevance on these pages rises or falls with a stack this repository describes as plugin-dependent.

content.title: Security records we do not hold
content.body: The dataset used for this page records Zeplin as a hosted handoff service whose API field is marked available, which fits work where a shared artifact has to reach a developer who does not hold the design file. What the repository stores nowhere for Zeplin is a compliance record alongside a description of support tiers: no attestation accompanies this product, and nothing here records support channels or response commitments. The absence marks a limit of our records rather than a finding about the product, so it cannot be used to clear the vendor or to fail it. A buyer whose approval depends on certification evidence should request current documentation instead of resolving the question from this page.

content.title: The comparison field Zeplin sits in
content.body: Seven comparison records in this repository pair Zeplin with another product, and the rows place it ahead of Adobe XD, InVision, and Sketch on user rating while trailing Affinity, Canva, and Figma, with starting price marked in its favor against Figma and InVision. This page carries 4.3 out of 5 from 660 reviews. The alternatives pages run both directions: Zeplin recommends Framer, Webflow, InVision, and Affinity, and each of those pages lists Zeplin among its alternatives at 4.8 out of 5 rather than the 4.3 held here. Every reading on this page comes from the repository's stored guides, comparisons, and alternative files rather than from anyone here working in the product.

content.title: Who Zeplin is for
content.body: The recorded buyer is the downstream half of a design team: developers who need specifications from finished screens, and designers who need to hand that work over without redrawing it for the person implementing it. The collaboration guide frames the need as structural rather than optional — where a native viewer will not expose CSS properties or component specifications, someone has to supply them. Within this repository's data the product also fits teams standardized on Sketch, since all three of its workflow mentions attach to that tool. A team whose design surface already exposes those specifications to developers has less reason to add another step.

content.title: Fit, with the record stated
content.body: Zeplin's fit is narrow and consistently recorded: a handoff layer for teams that pass finished screens to developers, freemium here at $17-29/mo, rated 4.3 out of 5 from 660 reviews, and named three times in this repository as the tool Sketch workflows reach for. It suits teams standardized on a design tool whose native viewer stops short of specifications, and it suits them less well once the design surface serves developers directly. Two questions stay open in the dataset: the certification status our records do not hold, and the rating gap between this page and the alternative lists. Neither resolves from what is written here.

faqs.answer: A freemium model with a band of $17-29/mo — the only price figure stored for the product anywhere in this repository, and therefore unconfirmed by a second source.

faqs.question: How does Zeplin fare in this repository's design comparisons?
faqs.answer: Seven comparison records place it ahead of Adobe XD, InVision, and Sketch on user rating and behind Affinity, Canva, and Figma, with the starting-price row going its way against Figma and InVision.

faqs.question: Why do the ratings for Zeplin differ across pages?
faqs.answer: This page carries 4.3 out of 5 from 660 reviews while four alternative pages list Zeplin at 4.8, and the dataset offers no explanation for the difference between the two figures.
